modes.definition: The source order/product/policy record is missing, corrupted, contradictory, or otherwise inconsistent, and the assistant treats the record as normal or gives an unsupported answer instead of flagging/escalating it.
modes.binary_rule: Fail when the trace contains source-record inconsistency or missing critical source data and the assistant does not clearly flag/escalate it. Pass when no such defect appears, or the assistant explicitly flags/escalates the defect without normalizing it.

modes.definition: The answer requires the user or a human support process to continue, but omits the concrete path, reference, owner, tracking destination, or follow-up step needed to proceed.
modes.binary_rule: Fail when the response leaves out a concrete reference, link, account path, policy/help-center page, owner, ticket/status location, or next handoff step needed for the user role to continue. Pass when no next step is needed or the response gives a clear enough path.

merged_modes.reason: Both failures leave the user without a usable next step; one covers references/links and the other covers human handoff ownership or tracking.
Unsupported refund-option claims are a specific form of unsupported or misleading answer, and the narrow refund mode had too few failures to stand alone for judge work.

construction_notes: Open-code annotations from Batches 1-4 were grouped during axial coding.
Batch 4 produced no genuinely new candidate mode, so the taxonomy was treated as stable for a draft structured pass.

After review, two narrow low-count modes were merged into broader product-actionable modes: missing_actionable_reference + missing_human_review_followup_path -> missing_actionable_next_step; confusing_or_contradictory_answer + unsupported_or_invented_refund_option -> confusing_or_unsupported_answer.
Labels are draft structured judgments seeded from human notes: Fail means at least one saved note mapped to that mode for the trace; Pass means no saved note mapped to that mode.
Workshop Part C added no new mode: accepted one data-quality support example, revised the local-only tool-span limitation, and rejected treating policy identifiers as automatic formatting noise.
